description: Classification of every leaf of the BuilderGate server configuration schema. Pinned against the Zod schema by server/src/schemas/settingsInventory.test.ts, which derives the leaf set at run time via listConfigSchemaLeafPaths.
classificationPrecedenceNote: A leaf can satisfy more than one description; exactly one classification is recorded, chosen by this precedence. inert wins first because a leaf with no consumer cannot meaningfully be anything else. reserved wins next so that the keys RuntimeConfigStore names in RESERVED_WAVE6_SETTING_KEYS keep the classification that table already assigns them. safety-only then captures leaves whose role is to bound or deny, including some that are editable; editableInSettings records that overlap rather than hiding it.
consumerDiscovery: Consumers are admitted by two rules, and every consumer records which one admitted it in its `match` field. `dotted-path`: the module contains an access chain that resolves to this leaf. That is one of three forms — the leaf's last two or more path segments written as member access (`twoFactor.issuer`, `ws.outputCoalesceWindowMs`, including `?.` and `['leaf']` spellings); a member access `X.leaf` whose receiver names the section (`authConfig.jwtSecret`) or is a generic config holder (`config`, `cfg`, `settings`, `options`, `limits`, or an identifier ending in one of those) in a module that names the section as a whole word or carries it in its own path (`this.config.certPath` in SSLService.ts); or a destructuring binding of the leaf out of such a source (`const { certPath, keyPath, caPath } = this.config`). `co-occurrence`: the module merely mentions the leaf's last path segment AND its immediate parent segment (for a top-level leaf, the top-level section name) as whole words somewhere in the same file, with no access chain anywhere. Where a leaf has any `dotted-path` match, its `co-occurrence` candidates are discarded, so a `co-occurrence` entry can appear only for a leaf with no access chain on the whole shipped surface. As of this derivation no entry is admitted by `co-occurrence`; the value stays in the vocabulary because the fallback is still reachable. Read both plainly. A `co-occurrence` entry is a place to START READING, not proof that the module consumes the value — it is only a locator. A `dotted-path` entry is far stronger but is still a locator, because a chain can appear in a comment, a log string or a regular expression, and because the `symbol` is the nearest preceding declaration at the match rather than a resolved binding. Searched: server/src, frontend/src, tools and server/tools. Excluded: the schema, the generated types, the config template, the schema-walk helper configSchemaLeaves.ts, test files and the monolithic test-runner, benchmark code under server/src/benchmarks, and the key-agnostic plumbing that mentions every leaf by construction (RuntimeConfigStore.ts, SettingsService.ts, ConfigFileRepository.ts, TerminalResourcePolicyInventory.ts, frontend/src/types/settings.ts). At most two consumers are recorded per leaf, listed in module-path order; where more than two qualified, shipped application code under server/src and frontend/src was preferred over build and ops scripts under tools. Two attributions were removed as confirmed false positives: server.port to McpNodeHttpListener.ts, which reads its own MCP `configRecord.port` and never `config.server.port`, and twoFactor.enabled to authRoutes.ts, where `twoFactor` occurs only in a comment and a log string. The authoritative check on whether a leaf still has a consumer at all is a fresh search of the shipped surface; the pinning test enforces coverage, classification and the `match` vocabulary, not symbol precision. resourceLimits.telemetry.recentEventLimit is recorded explicitly because its only consumer is inside RuntimeConfigStore itself, where it sets the telemetry ring capacity, and that module is excluded from discovery.
